@@126510116 <p> Save the Children has announced a fresh call for innovation partners as part of its Immunisation Accelerator , aimed at increasing vaccination rates among children in Nigeria and Ethiopia . <p> The initiative , backed by a $1 million grant from global healthcare company GSK , is focused on supporting bold , locally driven solutions to address persistent barriers that prevent children from accessing life-saving vaccines . <p> Now in its second round , the programme is open to a wide range of applicants , including community-based organisations , national and local NGOs , research teams , social enterprises , and tech companies operating in Nigeria and Ethiopia . <p> Selected applicants will receive up to $100,000 in funding per project , along with tailored technical support to help bring their innovations to life . <p> The initiative targets " zero dose " children , those who have never received a single routine vaccination . <p> These children are especially vulnerable to preventable diseases such as measles , cholera , and polio . Current estimates suggest that Nigeria has approximately 2.1 million zero-dose children , while Ethiopia is home @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ programme , successful applicants will also have the opportunity to pilot their innovations within existing vaccination efforts run by Save the Children in collaboration with GSK . <p> These pilot projects aim to improve both the supply and demand sides of immunisation by addressing logistical hurdles , raising awareness , and leveraging new technologies . <p> The Lead of the Save the Children Immunisation Accelerator , Ermias Teshome , emphasised the urgent need for inventive strategies in light of mounting global challenges . <p> " As conflicts , climate change , and other global challenges increasingly disrupt vaccination efforts , it 's clear that we need bold , new approaches to protect every child 's right to health . " <p> " Local innovation plays a critical role in overcoming both supply and demand barriers to immunisation . Through the Immunisation Accelerator , we are seeking scalable , context-driven solutions . We look forward to receiving fresh applications and ambitious thinking that push the boundaries of what innovation can achieve . " <p> Chief Global Health Officer , GSK , Thomas Breuer , echoed this sentiment , underscoring the importance @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ support Save the Children 's leadership in driving innovative , locally led solutions to improve childhood vaccination rates in Ethiopia and Nigeria . " <p> " The local knowledge and capabilities generated from Save the Children 's Immunisation Accelerator , funded through a grant from GSK , are already yielding promising approaches with the potential to help transform health outcomes for children not only in these regions , but globally . It 's inspiring to see how this initiative is shaping a healthier future , helping us get ahead of disease together , " Breuer added . <p> Among the first round of grantees is Ethiopia-based HABTech Solutions PLC , awarded nearly $100,000 for a digital solution that uses data analytics and visualisation tools to improve immunisation decision-making and tackle the challenges surrounding zero-dose children . <p> The second round of applications is now open , offering a new wave of innovators the chance to join this growing effort to ensure that no child is left behind when it comes to essential vaccines .

This momentum is partly driven by the introduction of the African Continental Free Trade Area ( AfCFTA ) and various platforms designed to help Africans better understand and access each other 's products . In his closing speech , Professor Oramah highlighted an interesting example : sometimes one African country imports goods from thousands of kilometres away , even though the same product is made just next door -- without realising it . For instance , a buyer might travel all the way to China to purchase rubber , even though that rubber is produced by a neighbouring country , with China sourcing the same product from that neighbour . He died in August 2024 at age 95 @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ " Sonny Ramphal will also be remembered as a great advocate of the efforts by the developing countries of the South to persuade the richer developed countries of the North to contribute more effectively to the development of the countries of the South , " adding : " It was in this respect that he played a prominent role in the Brandt Commission that was set up in 1977 on international development issues chaired by the former Chancellor of Germany , Willy Brandt . " <p> Continuing , he described Sonny Ramphal " as a man with great oratorical skills and word-craft ; a remarkable Foreign Minister of his native Guyana and a great player in the affairs of his Caribbean region ; a global diplomat who rendered enduring service to the Commonwealth ; indeed , an icon of the modern Commonwealth . " <p> Attendees at the service included the representative of HM King Charles III , the British Foreign Secretary , a number of Commonwealth High Commissioners and representatives of Commonwealth organizations <p> Anyaoku recalled how he first met Sonny Ramphal in August 1972 at the meeting of @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Guyana , which he hosted and Chaired . <p> " The first Commonwealth Secretary-General , Arnold Smith , had sent me then Director of the Commonwealth Secretariat 's Political Affairs Division as an Observer to the meeting , " Anyaoku said , noting : " Sonny 's brilliance in conducting the meeting and his bonhomie made a lasting impression on me , and on a number of Foreign Ministers with whom I talked during the meeting . " <p> " The first Commonwealth Secretary-General , Arnold Smith , is rightly credited with consolidating the evolution of the British Commonwealth into the Commonwealth of sovereign independent nations as envisaged in the London Declaration of 1949 , and also with the beginning of the formal articulation of the fundamental principles of the Commonwealth with the Singapore Declaration of 1971 , which was followed by the Harare Declaration of 1991 and culminated in the Commonwealth Charter signed by The Queen in 2013 , " Anyaoku noted . <p> The Commonwealth of Nations is an association @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ former British colonies , now with an estimated combined population of 2.6 billion , almost a third of the world 's population , with 2.1 billion living in India and 95% in Africa and Asia combined . <p> Francophone African nations of Gabon and Togo have also joined the Commonwealth , along with Mozambique and Rwanda , all of which had no prior historical relationship with the United Kingdom . <p> This makes the Commonwealth a mosaic union of diverse people , cultures , traditions , and religions from the smallest and developing to some of the most developed countries in the world . <p> The first Secretary-General , Arnold Smith of Canada ( 1965-1975 ) is " credited with laying the foundations as the first Secretary-General , " establishing the Secretariat 's systems and global role . @@126854019 <h> Why Nigeria must retire its political geriarchy <p> By : Cynthia C. Umezulike <p> Date : 10 Jul 2025 <p> Share : <p> I rarely write about Nigeria anymore . Not because I have stopped caring -- far from it but because it has become emotionally exhausting to grieve the same loss over and over again . Nigeria is a country that routinely betrays those who dare to believe in its promise . And yet , despite all evidence to the contrary , some of us still do . <p> But every now and again , something triggers the ache anew . This week , it was the celebration -- yes , celebration -- of the African Democratic Congress ( ADC ) , a party now functioning more as a retirement home for Nigeria 's politically fatigued than a vehicle for real national transformation . I saw the fanfare , the speeches , the familiar faces , the calculated handshakes -- and I felt that same old nausea return . I asked myself , not for the first time : How long will this charade continue ? We see @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ The names change ; the rot remains . <p> How do non-senile Nigerians still stomach this ? We must speak plainly . The ADC , like so many other parties before it , is little more than a conglomerate of power-hungry , relevance-chasing old men . Men who should be in elder forums offering moral guidance , not masquerading as saviours of a nation they helped bring to its knees . These are not leaders with a vision for the 21st century -- they are relics of a bygone era , desperately clinging to influence in a world that has already moved on . <p> This is not ageism . It is realism . No progressive nation is led indefinitely by a class of leaders who have outlived their political creativity , moral courage , and intellectual relevance . At some point , generational transition becomes not just desirable , but inevitable . Nigeria , however , seems determined to defy even this most basic truth of democratic evolution . Instead , we recycle the same tired political figures under different party names and with slightly altered talking points , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ through it . These men -- many of whom have shuffled from one party to the next like players in a never-ending game of political musical chairs -- are not concerned with governance . They are concerned with access : to contracts , to titles , to security votes , to power . That is the only continuity they understand . Nation-building ? That 's for the campaign slogans . <p> And still , they gather . In hotels , in halls , in front of microphones , issuing grand pronouncements about saving Nigeria -- as though we 've forgotten the decades they spent mismanaging it . It 's not just insulting ; it 's tragic . Because for every recycled statesman elevated by the media and welcomed back into party machinery , there are hundreds of brilliant , competent young Nigerians locked out of the political process . <p> This is perhaps the greatest tragedy of all . Nigeria is brimming with talent . From tech innovators and climate activists to policy analysts and social entrepreneurs -- our youth are among the most dynamic in the world . They @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ in Enugu , reshaping fintech in Abuja , and winning scholarships at Oxford and MIT . But when it comes to political power , they are systematically excluded -- treated as errand boys and protocol girls in a system that does n't take them seriously . <p> Why ? Because youth threatens the monopoly . A young Ibrahim Tour ? ( symbolic or real ) would never survive a day in the ADC , or any of the older parties for that matter . He would ask too many questions . He would challenge the status quo . He would demand real change . And that makes him dangerous . And so , the system pushes him out -- or never lets him in . <h> Related News <p> Let me be clear : the problem is not just the ADC . It 's the entire culture of gatekeeping , of feudal politics disguised as democracy . It 's the willful exclusion of the competent in favour of the compliant . Every time these political dinosaurs mount a podium , a thousand brilliant young Nigerians lose faith in the system @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , and feed other nations with the genius we refused to water . <p> Nigeria is , at this moment , at a crossroads . The challenges we face are existential : climate change , mass unemployment , debt distress , food insecurity , systemic corruption , and a complete breakdown of trust between citizens and institutions . These are not problems that can be solved with nostalgia . They require vision , courage , and -- most importantly -- fresh thinking . <p> But instead , we are served the same cold leftovers . The same alliances of godfathers and political jobbers , reuniting not to save Nigeria , but to save their own fading relevance . <p> It is not enough to simply register new political parties or change slogans . What we need is a total reimagining of what leadership looks like in this country . And that starts with political will -- not to cling to power , but to hand it over . Not to anointed sons and cronies , but to a new generation of Nigerians with ideas , integrity , and imagination . @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ logic of democratic survival . We often say , " The youth are the leaders of tomorrow . " But that tomorrow will never come unless we fight for it . The current gatekeepers will not open the door voluntarily -- they must be pushed aside by a citizenry that is no longer content to clap for speeches and queue for rice at rallies . Civil society , the media , the diaspora , the private sector -- we must all demand better . We must insist that merit replaces mediocrity , that youth is not equated with inexperience , and that public office is not treated as personal inheritance . <p> Achebe was right . " There was once a country . " What he did n't say -- perhaps because it was too painful -- is that the country he mourned is fast becoming unrecoverable . But maybe , just maybe , a new one can still be born . A country led not by those who destroyed the old , but by those with the courage to imagine something entirely different . <p> Nigeria must retire its @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ free them -- and us -- from the prison of nostalgia . The time for mentorship is now . The time for succession is overdue . Because if we continue down this path , clapping for men who should be writing memoirs instead of manifestos , then we are not just betraying our youth -- we are condemning them to a future even bleaker than our past . And we will have no one left to blame but ourselves . <p> There was a country . But today , there is only the illusion of one -- maintained by a fragile alliance of men too proud to admit their time is over . @@127082238 <h> Artivism and children 's manifesto on climate change <p> Sustainability is a concept that refers to meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs . Indeed , the young citizens of today need to understand climate change , circular economy , renewable energy and other relevant ideas to take up the baton for tomorrow . <p> The voices of children and young people , especially in the developing world , must be acknowledged and included , as they are the ones who will ultimately live with the consequences of the decisions and actions we take today . This is why the Connecting Communities and Heritages against Climate Change programme has come at the right time . A portmanteau word that combines ' art ' and ' activism ' , artivism refers to where artistic practices are used to promote social or political change . @@127082314 <h> Flooding and property loss in Nigeria : Case for urgent action <p> By : Amos Jolaoye <p> Date : 17 Jul 2025 <p> Share : <p> What was once viewed primarily as a natural or humanitarian issue has now evolved into a pressing threat to real estate investment , infrastructure , and sustainable urban development across the country . <p> Flooding occurs when water overflows onto land that is typically dry , often due to heavy rainfall , inadequate drainage systems , or overflowing rivers . However , beyond natural causes , it is essential to acknowledge the man-made dimensions of this crisis . Poor urban planning , lack of maintenance of public infrastructure , and a general absence of proactive policy implementation have significantly worsened the situation . <p> For those of us working in the property and building sector , it is critical to stop viewing flooding merely as an environmental issue . The damages caused by floodwaters are not only structural but also economic and reputational . When water enters buildings , it weakens foundations , damages walls , ruins electrical systems , and renders properties @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , and in some cases , the damage is irreversible . Consequently , properties located in flood-prone areas suffer from sharp declines in market value . Investors shy away from high-risk zones , and buyers become cautious , leaving property owners in a difficult position . <p> The financial implications go further . Banks and lending institutions are becoming increasingly wary of financing developments in areas with a known history of flooding . Mortgage approvals are delayed or denied outright , reducing access to financing and hindering overall market liquidity . Insurance is another concern . <p> Urban flooding in Nigeria is most commonly caused by pluvial flooding , which occurs when rainfall exceeds the capacity of existing drainage systems . This is particularly dangerous in densely populated urban areas , where the soil is already covered by concrete and can not absorb excess water . When drainage systems are blocked or poorly maintained , water has nowhere to go , resulting in swift and destructive floods . <p> A recent example from Ondo State provides a sobering lesson . Heavy rains left hundreds of families displaced , homes destroyed @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ This tragic event highlights how quickly and easily real estate assets can be wiped out when systemic infrastructure issues are ignored . Unfortunately , this is not a distant concern -- it is a direct warning for Lagos , particularly areas like Gbagada . <h> Related News <p> In Gbagada , the major drainage channel has not been cleared in over a year . As of July , this year , it is nearly filled , with no sign of government intervention . With the rainy season nearing its peak , Gbagada is on the verge of another preventable disaster . This problem is not unique to Gbagada . Across Lagos -- from Lekki to Ikorodu -- blocked drainages are silently threatening communities . The question we must all ask is whether we are going to wait for another avoidable tragedy before taking meaningful action . <p> Addressing the flood crisis requires a unified and coordinated effort across the public and private sectors . The government must prioritise routine maintenance of drainage systems and invest in long-term flood control infrastructure . @@127082830 <h> Nigeria joins BRICS for new global order <p> BRICS refers to the economic bloc formed by Brazil , Russia , India , China , and South Africa . The acronym comprises initial letters of the founding countries that gave birth to the group . After the initial proposal by economist Jim O'Neill of Goldman Sachs in 2001 to use the initial letters of founding member nations as an acronym for the body , BRICS would evolve through a series of discussions focused on promoting economic cooperation and coordination , among major emerging global economies . <p> The main goals of BRICS are , among others , geared towards strengthening economic , political , and social cooperation , including advancing the influence of the Global South in broadening international affairs , promoting sustainable development and social inclusion . The first BRIC Summit that took place in Yekaterinburg , Russia , in 2008 was without South Africa . It was only in 2010 , nine years after the first summit , that South Africa joined , thereby expanding BRIC to BRICS . <p> Being an economic bloc that seeks economic advancement @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ is hinged on strengthening economic cooperation , especially in the area of stimulating trade , investment , and engendering financial cooperation among members , in a bid to create an equitable multipolar global economy . Apart from economic goals , the BRICS platform avails member countries of pursuing political and diplomatic coordination for the mutual interest and benefits to member countries , the group provides a platform for political dialogue and coordination on issues of mutual interest , allowing member countries to present a united front on global matters and advocate the interests of developing nations . <p> In a bid to achieve its objectives of create a new world order that gives developing countries another podium to advance their growth and improvements of their citizens , BRICS holds regular summits where member countries ' leaders meet to deliberate and make decisions on key issues . The group has also created several mechanisms for cooperation among member countries , including the New Development Bank ( NDB ) for financial collaboration , among others . Apart from conducting various meetings at both ministerial and expert levels on various topics covering finance @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ extended invitations to Nigeria , Saudi Arabia , Egypt , Ethiopia , Iran , Argentina , and the United Arab Emirates ( UAE ) to join the bloc as partners . <p> At the 2025 BRICS Summit that took place in Rio de Janeiro , Brazil , between 6th-7th July , after the admission of Nigeria as the 9th member of the group in January , 2025 , President Bola Ahmed Tinubu honoured BRICS ' invitation to attend the 17th BRICS Summit where the high-level leaders ' meeting adopted 126 commitments on global governance , finance , health , artificial intelligence , climate change , among other strategic areas . Re-affirming their commitment to the group , BRICS Leaders reiterated their " mutual respect and understanding , sovereign equality , solidarity , democracy , openness , inclusion , collaboration and consensus " among member countries . The leaders ' meeting also resolved to extend their " commitment to strengthening cooperation within the expanded BRICS , based on three pillars of cooperation : politics and security , economy and finance , and cultural and people-to-people cooperation . We are also enhancing @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , a fairer and more representative international order , a revitalised and reformed multilateral system , sustainable development , and inclusive growth " . <p> One of the 126 commitments agreed by the leaders of the 11 largest emerging economies is strengthening efforts towards the promotion of consultations among BRICS member countries in a bid to realise a just and fair global governance and forging mutually beneficial relations among nations , adding , " We want to emphasise the importance of the Global South as a driver of positive change , especially amid significant international challenges -- including escalating geopolitical tensions , economic slowdown , accelerated technological transformation , protectionist measures and migration challenges " . <p> The invitation extended to Nigeria to become a member of the group underscored the importance BRICS attaches to the country as the world 's sixth most populous nation and one of the largest economies in Africa . President Tinubu 's support for BRICS is seen as reflecting the relevance of the group in forging a new economic alliance anchored on mutual benefits , including creating platforms for global collaborations and cooperation . Harping @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ that member countries of BRICS must be architects of their future . <p> We commend the recently concluded summit in Brazil that brought together leaders of 11 emerging economies and the formal admission of Nigeria as a member . Blueprint hopes that the creditable objectives of BRICS anchored on global cooperation and collaborations shall translate into economic advantage and the emergence of a new global order for not only Nigeria , but also other member countries , including other developing nations . @@127161465 <p> Nigeria 's local government system has been the subject of numerous reforms , intended to bring governance closer to the people and foster grassroots development . However , these reforms have often fallen short of their lofty goals . There have been recurring themes of unfulfilled promises and persistent challenges that have plagued the local government landscape . From issues of inadequate funding and corruption to political interference and capacity deficits , we delve into the complexities that continue to hinder the effectiveness and autonomy of local governments , leaving a trail of dashed hopes and unmet needs in communities across the nation . SAMUEL OGIDAN , NICHOLAS UWERUNONYE , INNOCENT OWEH , VICTORIA OJUGBANA and KAZEEM AWOJOODU report <p> One year after the initial surge of renewed attention on local gov ? ernment reforms , the landscape in Nigeria remains complex and uneven . While the Supreme Court 's land ? mark judgment in July 2024 , affirming the financial autonomy of Nigeria 's 774 Local Government Councils and prohib ? iting state governments from interfering with local government funds and estab ? lishing caretaker committees , generated widespread optimism , the overall impact and long-term viability of these reforms remain uncertain . Across the nation , Nigerians from diverse backgrounds have voiced concerns that the promise of effective grassroots governance is yet to be realised . <p> A major source of contention is the fate of local government chairmen and their operational autonomy . Are they truly empowered to serve their com ? munities , or are they merely puppets of state governors ? How do they operate in political terrain , particularly in a climate marked by defections motivated by sec ? ond-term ambitions ? And ultimately , how are local government areas truly thriving , and what factors influence their success ? <p> Comrade Rotimi Agboluaje , a policy analyst , Associate of the Nigerian Insti ? tute of Public Relations ( ANIPR ) , and Public Relations Officer ( PRO ) of the Nigerian Economic Society ( NES ) , Oyo State chapter , captures the sentiment of many when he notes that the Supreme Court verdict was " widely applauded by many Nigerians " due to the importance of local government at the grassroots level . <p> However , he adds , " One year later , there is a stalemate . The practicality of the verdict and local autonomy is not fea ? sible due to many factors , ranging from le ? gal , constitutional , cultural , and political to administrative encumbrances . " <p> The issue of autonomy , coupled with funding constraints and a lack of inde ? pendence from the grip of state govern ? ments , has been linked to major challeng ? es facing the effectiveness of government at the local level . Section 162 of the 1999 Constitution , which stipulates a joint account between the state and its local councils , remains a significant stumbling block . " Until the section is amended , the issue of local government autonomy will remain a mirage , " Agboluaje emphasises . <p> The extent to which local government chairmen are subject to undue influence by state governors is a recurring theme . " Most council chairmen are subject to undue influence of the state governor as they are at their beck and call , operating at their whims and caprices , " Agboluaje asserts . This dependence undermines their ability to act in the best interests of their constituents and hinders grassroots development . Even if autonomy were granted on paper , Agboluaje questions its real-world impact , suggesting that " most of them might still want to submit their authority to the state governors for politi ? cal convenience and subservience . There may be no significant change , as most of them would be hampered by ineptitude and maladministration . " <p> In Oyo State , for example , Agboluaje claims that " local governments are nearly non-existent . Immediately after the apex court 's verdict , the council chiefs came together to pledge allegiance to Gover ? nor Seyi Makinde . " This highlights the pervasive culture of subservience that undermines the very essence of local government autonomy . <p> Mr. Olawale Ogunbusola , a Fellow of the Eccolerite Institute for Peace Ad ? vancement ( FEIPA ) , author , and social commentator , echoes these concerns . He describes the Supreme Court judgment as having received a " setback , " citing the " la ? cuna " in the 1999 Nigerian Constitution , as amended , that Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State is yet to address . Ogunbusola argues that the " failure of functionality of the local government administration has had a great negative impact on the grass ? roots people , promoting corruption and conspiracy among the local government administrators , as this does not reflect ac ? countability and good governance . " <p> He believes that " local government autonomy is yet to be operational " and will require " political will " from state governors to remove the " lasso against grassroots development . " <p> Public analyst Adeola Badru paints a similar picture . He notes that while Nige ? ria operates a three-tier federal structure on paper , " in practice , the autonomy of local government chairmen is often at the mercy of state governors . " Badru contends that speculation about the op ? erational autonomy of local government chairmen is " not just widespread , it is now an open secret amongst the citizens . " <p> In today 's political climate , marked by defections motivated by second-term ambitions , the fate of local government chairmen hangs precariously . Badru ex ? plains that " many are forced to toe the line of state governors or risk being removed , sidelined , or denied party tickets , thereby weakening accountability and undermin ? ing development planning , as chairmen often prioritise political survival over grassroots governance and well-being . " <p> Florence Okah-Avae , a human rights advocate and managing director of Flow Communications Company , Lagos , pro ? ducers of Tech Hub on Unilag Radio , underscores the extent of the problem . " Governance at the local government level is indeed in shambles and plagued by several challenges that hinder its effec ? tiveness , " she says . She points to the heavy reliance on state and federal government allocations , which makes it " nearly im ? possible to make independent decisions and implement policies that are peculiar to them . " Even with the Supreme Court ruling of July 2024 , she argues that " state governors still exert much control over their allocations . " <p> Okah-Avae also laments the " rate of corruption and mismanagement of the available resources meant for develop ? ment , which are most of the time diverted to the pockets of corrupt officials , making it difficult to see expected visible progress within the local government areas . " She says that the situation is evident in the " abandoned projects " and " shabbily exe ? cuted " infrastructure like roads , schools , and hospitals . She concludes that state governors exert a " significant influence over local government chairmen and lo ? cal government affairs , often using their positions to dictate decisions , hindering progress and autonomy . " <p> Wale Ogunade , a lawyer and human rights advocate , echoes the sentiment , stating that " there 's nothing that has happened in terms of the economy " since the Supreme Court ruling . He claims that local governments " have been under the grasp of the governor , and as a result , they would not want that grasp to slip out of their hands . " He believes that this is " why they have not allowed the implementation of the program , or project , or policy . " <p> Ogunade argues that local govern ? ment chairmen are " afraid that if they move it , any one of them who dares it will be a target of the governor or dare the wrath of the governor . " He suggests that " the only way out is for the press and civil society to start advocacy towards the implementation of the program . " <p> He warns that in the current politi ? cal climate , the fate of local government chairmen depends on their loyalty to the " winning team , " cautioning them to be " calculating and very careful because any false move will be to their detriment . " <p> Despite the pervasive challenges , some local governments are thriving . Their success is often attributed to a combina ? tion of strong leadership , community engagement , and relative freedom from excessive political interference . Badru notes that " in states where governors allow some degree of local initiative and despite state government 's interference , some Local Government Areas have been able to invest in primary health care , ed ? ucation , and road infrastructure in their locality . " <p> In Kwara State , urban councils like Ilorin West benefit from stronger inter ? nal revenue generation and community infrastructure , making them more viable under direct funding systems . Success factors include disciplined financial prac ? tices , avoidance of unnecessary political appointees , community oversight , and targeted use of funds for basic services . Where these governance principles are observed , LGAs show more promise . <p> Rotimi Agboluaje points out that " op ? portunities at the local government level are numerous . There are many markets , motor parks , and economic activities in the state . If they are allowed to collect rates and rents that are due to them , gov ? ernance would actually be closer to the people through their performance . " <p> Wale Ogunade believes that the drive for success " is from the chairman himself . If the chairman has a drive , the local gov ? ernment will boom , but if he does n't have a drive , definitely there 's nothing that will come out of it . " He also argues that grassroots orientation is crucial , stating that " since some of the local government chairmen are not grassroots-oriented , they can not serve the people because they play to the tune of their governors , who installed them . " <p> The challenges facing local govern ? ments in Nigeria are significant , ranging from funding and autonomy to political pressure and capacity gaps . Empower ? ing local governments through genuine reforms , transparent elections , and legis ? lative safeguards is crucial to unlocking their full potential . <p> As stakeholderlders continue to push for structural changes towards local gov ? ernment autonomy , the hope is that Ni ? geria will move closer to a system where local governance truly serves the people , especially at the grassroots level . <p> Adeola Badru emphasises that local government chairmen must leverage their unique understanding of commu ? nity needs to implement effective policies and engage citizens in meaningful ways . " By fostering transparency and account ? ability , they can build trust and support within their communities , " he says . <p> Florence Okah-Avae stresses the need for local government chairmen to " find creative and innovative ways to revenue generation capacity , distribution , and control to improve governance that will enhance citizen engagement . " <p> Wale Ogunade believes that the oppor ? tunities for local government chairmen lie in their ability to perform . " Once they are able to perform , definitely they will put their names on the national calendar or national spot , " he says . <p> The Call for Devolution and Constitu ? tional Reform <p> For local government autonomy to truly become a reality , many believe that more fundamental changes are needed . Timothy Osadolor , Deputy National Youth Leader of the Peoples Democratic Party ( PDP ) , argues that " until we have a complete devolution of power , this issue will continue to linger . " He criticises Presi ? dent Tinubu for " playing politics " with the issue instead of enforcing the Supreme Court judgment . <p> Nigeria , a country brimming with potential , is experiencing a worsening human rights crisis . From government crackdowns on dissent and free expression to rampant police brutality and extra-judicial killings , the country is on a dangerous path to repression and systematic violations that endanger citizens ' fundamental rights and freedoms . ROLAND OGBONNAYA , TITILOPE JOSEPH , and SEYI TAIWO-OGUNTUASE report . <p> Cries for justice are growing loud in Nigeria , but instead of soothing support , they are increasingly met with silence , intimidation , and violence . A surge in human rights violations has cast a pall over the country , prompting harsh warnings from human rights advocates and painting a bleak picture of a society struggling under the weight of poverty , impunity , and governance failure . <p> The National Human Rights Commission ( NHRC ) recently issued a chilling report : over 320,000 cases of human rights violations were reported in June alone , highlighting the Nigerian state 's growing fragility and erosion of basic rights . <p> " We received 327,154 complaints in June , reflecting another sharp increase in human rights violations , each one a desperate plea for justice and a stark reminder of how much work remains to be done , " said Dr. Tony Ojukwu , Executive Secretary of the NHRC , during the presentation of the June 2025 Human Rights Situation Dashboard in Abuja . His words , heavy with concern , were a stark indictment of the current situation . <p> Dr. Ojukwu lamented the reports ' recurring nature , emphasising the urgency of the situation . " Every month , when we come together to present this human rights dashboard , we are confronted with the sobering reality of those affected by violence , injustice , discrimination , and systemic neglect , " he said . <p> " These figures compel us to reflect deeply on our collective responsibility and ask the difficult question : are we doing enough ? The events of June 2025 call for not only reflection , but also an honest and timely response . " <p> The NHRC report detailed several particularly heinous incidents that heighten the severity of the crisis . Among them were the brutal attacks on the Yelewata and Dauda communities in Benue State 's Guma Local Government Area , which killed over 200 people . " Fathers , mothers , children , and breadwinners ; families ripped apart , livelihoods destroyed , and futures extinguished in moments of senseless brutality , " Dr. Ojukwu described the victims solemnly . <p> The commission was also deeply concerned about the rise in attacks on law enforcement and local security forces . More than 17 soldiers were allegedly killed in coordinated attacks in Kaduna and Niger states , further destabilising already fragile regions . The massacre of more than 40 Civilian Joint Task Force ( CJTF ) members in Ruggar Chida was another devastating blow . <p> " Their deaths leave a void in local security structures , making civilians even more vulnerable to more violence , " Dr. Ojukwu noted and stressed the importance of community-based forces in protecting vulnerable populations . <p> The NHRC report also highlighted the growing insecurity on Nigerian highways , making travel a terrifying gamble . " In June alone , more than 50 travellers were kidnapped along major transit routes in Kogi and Benue states , " Dr. Ojukwu said . " These are not isolated criminal acts ; they directly violate the fundamental rights to free movement , economic participation , and personal dignity . " He emphasised the long-term trauma inflicted on victims and their families , as well as the public 's loss of confidence in road safety . <p> The NHRC is advocating a multifaceted approach to the crisis , urging the government to implement " decisive and coordinated security interventions . " Dr. Ojukwu also urged civil society and the media to provide " sustained advocacy and amplification of these issues , " as well as increased collaboration with development partners to address the underlying causes of these violations . <p> " This dashboard must not only serve as a record of tragedies , but also as a catalyst for meaningful and long-term change , " Dr. Ojukwu insisted . " Let us never forget that every complaint documented and statistics recorded in these dashboards represents a Nigerian citizen , a fellow human being looking for justice , safety , and the fulfilment of their basic rights . " <p> He reaffirmed the National Human Rights Commission 's dedication to its mission , saying the organisation " remains unwavering in its mandate to promote , protect , and enforce human rights throughout Nigeria . " <p> For human rights lawyers and activists on the ground , the NHRC 's report confirms what they have long observed : a slow but steady erosion of rights fuelled by a combination of factors such as government complicity , elite abuse of power , and law enforcement agencies ' failure to operate within the law . <p> Kabir Akingbolu , a human rights lawyer , paints a disturbing picture of a system in which the powerful routinely use state institutions to target ordinary citizens . " The rules governing security agencies exist , but they are routinely broken by the so-called big shots in society , " Akingbolu stated . " You see cases where a simple private misunderstanding -- like repeatedly texting someone -- is blown out of proportion when someone powerful uses the police to label it cyber-bullying , a crime with severe consequences . Law enforcement should protect citizens , not used to harm them . " <p> He stated that Nigeria 's rising poverty and economic hardship have made citizens more vocal about their dissatisfaction , but instead of addressing these concerns , the government has responded with repression . This , he claimed , is a violation of the government 's constitutional obligation to protect citizens ' rights and ensure their welfare . <p> Akingbolu also lamented the courts ' slow response to human rights violations . " Human rights cases are supposed to be treated urgently , given priority over other cases , and resolved quickly . However , in practice , the courts delay the cases as they would any other matter . Victims wait indefinitely for justice , and lawyers fighting these cases are frequently treated with contempt . " <p> He shared personal accounts of how human rights lawyers are harassed and discouraged in the courts . " Some judges look at human rights lawyers as troublemakers , wondering why we bother challenging these violations . It becomes so frustrating that you question whether filing fundamental rights cases is even worthwhile . Many of your cases are repeatedly adjourned without resolution , leaving victims without justice . <p> Despite these obstacles , Akingbolu urged lawyers to remain dedicated to defending the oppressed , emphasising the significance of pro bono work in safeguarding fundamental rights . <p> " As lawyers , we have a responsibility to advocate for the voiceless , even if the system frustrates us . We must take on these cases , regardless of whether we are compensated . Many victims of rights violations can not afford legal representation , so it is our moral and professional responsibility to intervene . " <p> He calls on the judiciary to uphold its constitutional responsibility and protect citizens ' rights from abuses by both the government and private individuals . " The courts need to stop playing it safe . They should make bold decisions against the government and its agencies when violations occur . Until this happens , human rights violations will continue to escalate . We need a judiciary that is fearless , swift , and equitable . " <p> Another human rights lawyer and activist , Femi Aborisade , attributes the increase in human rights violations to a fundamental governance failure . " Empirical studies and historical experience show that the higher the level of poverty in a society , the more likely repression , " he said . " Governments that are unable to meet their citizens ' basic existential needs will suppress democratic freedoms out of fear of opposition . " <p> Aborisade believes that when a government fails to provide for its citizens ' basic needs , such as food , shelter , healthcare , and employment , discontent grows , and in response , the government uses repressive tactics to silence protests and maintain a false sense of stability . <p> Aborisade criticised President Bola Tinubu 's Democracy Day speech , calling it deceptive and disconnected from reality . He used the recent detention of Comrade Andrew Emelieze , coordinator of the Federal Workers Forum , as a concrete example of the government 's hypocrisy . <p> " What kind of democracy are we talking about when a government claims to tolerate criticism while imprisoning a labour rights activist without due process ? " Aborisade asked . <p> He cautioned that no society can achieve peace by suppressing dissent . " The more you deny people their daily bread , the more they will protest . When they resist , the state 's only response has been brute force , not dialogue . " This is not sustainable . " <p> Aborisade urged Nigeria 's government to focus on addressing the root causes of unrest , such as poverty , unemployment , and social injustice , rather than using security forces to silence dissent . " We must stop pretending to practise democracy when what we see every day is authoritarianism dressed in democratic language . He warned that repression is not a sign of strength , but rather a symptom of failed governance . <p> Okechukwu Nwanguma , Executive Director of RULAAC , expressed similar concerns , stating that the NHRC 's report " reflects the terrifying scale of human rights violations in Nigeria , and it is unacceptable . " " Instead of protecting citizens , security agencies are the primary violators , illegally detaining individuals , torturing suspects , and violently suppressing dissent . The justice system is weak , and political leaders have been disturbingly silent , " Nwanguma stated . <p> Goddy Uwazurike , a lawyer and President of Credibility Group , identified a growing sense of impunity among violators as a major cause of the increase in abuses . He cited the use of the Cybercrime Act to intimidate citizens and restrict free speech . " Impunity is the rule of the day . Any post I make on Facebook or WhatsApp could land me in prison , " Uwazurike stated . <p> He painted a bleak picture of how arrests are carried out , comparing them to scenes from action films : heavily armed security agents storming homes , keeping suspects in secret detention facilities , and occasionally charging them in court . " The Human Rights Commission has been in a coma since Prof. Chidi Odinkalu left . The body sees no evil and hears no evil , " he complained . <p> He attributed the surge to poverty , poor governance , the proliferation of armed non-state actors , and a decline in civil society 's role in defending human rights . " Many groups focus solely on state actors , but violations committed by non-state actors are also increasing . " <p> Adeoye also stated that economic hardship has made it difficult for victims to seek legal redress . " Many poor Nigerians can not afford lawyers ' fees or even understand their rights . Lack of education is a major factor in their inability to resist or report violations . " <p> He acknowledged the NHRC 's limited capacity and advocated for greater collaboration with civil society organisations . He emphasised that human rights violations stem from a lack of access to healthcare , food , education , and housing , all of which are directly caused by poor government policies . <p> Wale Ogunade , a legal practitioner , agreed that Nigeria 's economic crisis has exacerbated the human rights situation . " Security agencies , which should protect citizens , are now exploiting them , " he claimed . <p> Ogunade described a recent incident in Surulere , Lagos , in which seven young men were arrested in front of their father 's house while chatting at 8 p.m . The police initially demanded N200,000 bail for each of them , a total of N1.4 million . After his intervention , the amount was negotiated down to N100,000 . " Fela used to sing about police stations becoming banks . That reality is more obvious now , " he stated . <p> He described security operatives , including private security agents , as enforcers of illegal activities . " They raid homes without warrants , seize phones , detain people on the streets under the guise of stop-and-frisk , and harass citizens over personal items such as money . " <p> According to Ogunade , increased media exposure and citizen vigilance can help to curb these excesses . " When people are aware of their rights and are willing to document abuses , it puts pressure on the authorities to act . " <p> The situation is dire , but hope remains . Experts are advocating a radical shift in strategy , emphasising government accountability , institutional reforms , and citizen empowerment . <p> " The Nigerian government must urgently end this culture of impunity by prosecuting offenders , empowering oversight bodies such as the NHRC , and ensuring that human rights are upheld in both law and practice , " Nwanguma stated . " We need leadership that protects citizens , not one that allows abuses to occur . Anything less would be a betrayal of the constitution and the people . " <p> Uwazurike believes that restoring the rule of law , enforcing court orders , and eliminating selective justice are critical steps towards resolving the crisis . " We need a responsible judiciary and punishment for acts of impunity as a deterrent , " he said . <p> Adeoye emphasised the importance of properly training security personnel , including the Amotekun and Hisbah corps , in human rights and constitutional justice . He advocated for human rights desks in police stations and the army , operational public defender units in the Justice Ministry , and faster judicial processes . <p> Ogunade encouraged citizens to use social media as a tool for accountability . " Video evidence posted online frequently reaches people with authority who can intervene . In the case of the traditional ruler who humiliated an elderly man , social media came to the rescue . " <p> He encouraged Nigerians to document and report incidents of abuse . " Once a violation is made public , there is a better chance of justice . Our most effective tools are awareness , vigilance , and solidarity . " <p> Until these issues are addressed , the voices of the vulnerable will continue to be silenced -- not by the law , but by the very institutions designed to protect them . The question remains : will Nigeria rise to the challenge and reaffirm its commitment to human rights , or will it continue to descend into repression ? The answer is found in the actions of its leaders , the bravery of its citizens , and the unwavering dedication of those who fight for justice . <p> Establishing military camps in Benue State offers a potential solution to the worsening insecurity exacerbating the ongoing food crisis . The aim of increasing military presence is to curb farmer-herder clashes , banditry , and other violence that disrupt agricultural activities and hinder food production and distribution . By providing a safer environment , the military camps could enable farmers to return to their land , cultivate crops , and contribute to alleviating the food crisis . The lack of political will , particularly in en ? forcing existing laws , has emboldened perpetrators , " he explained . <p> Ihomun , for his part , stated that " what is happening in Benue State is nothing short of a systematic genocide , a calculated campaign by armed Fulani herdsmen to displace our people and seize control of our ancestral lands . The goal is clear : to expel the indigenous Benue people using fear , violence , and terror . <p> " Unfortunately , the Benue State Gov ? ernment has failed in its constitutional duty to protect the lives and property of its citizens . Later , the blame shifted to religious lead ? ers . This series of denials and misdirec ? tion are not only unfortunate , but also dangerous , " he stated . <p> Ihomun , on the other hand , sees hope in the horizon , citing steps taken by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu during his visit to Benue in the aftermath of the Yelwata attack , such as ordering the ar ? rest of perpetrators and forming a Peace Committee to devise modalities for re ? solving lingering issues . <p> He stated , " President Bola Ahmed Tinubu stepped in with decisive leader ? ship , issuing a matching order to secu ? rity agencies to arrest the perpetrators and forming a Peace Committee . This is a promising development , and I believe peace can still be restored if bold and im ? mediate steps are taken , " he said . <p> Stroke , a devastating medical emergency where reduced blood flow to the brain causes brain cells to die , potentially leading to loss of function or death , is rapidly becoming a pandemic in Nigeria , demanding urgent attention and proactive measures . While often associated with old age , stroke can affect individuals of all ages , with alarming rates now observed even in younger population . The surge is fueled by a complex interplay of modifiable risk factors , limited access to healthcare , and deeply ingrained cultural beliefs that delay crucial intervention . <p> Professor Frank Imarhiagbe , a Consultant Neurologist and Professor of Medicine at the University of Benin Teaching Hospital ( UBTH ) Nigeria , gives insight into the subtle signs of stroke , the prevalence of the condition , and the challenges faced in diagnosing and treating it in Nigeria . <p> Understanding the Modifiable Risks : A Crucial Step Towards Prevention <p> Professor Imarhiagbe , who is also Head of the Stroke Unit at UBTH , emphasised the critical role of modifiable risk factors in stroke prevention . " Stroke is prevalent and it is getting worse because of the risk factors , " he explained . " The majority of stroke patients , two-thirds of them , have one of these modifiable risk factors . " The factors , unlike non-modifiable ones such as age and genetics , are within an individual 's power to control , offering a pathway to significantly reduce the risk of stroke . <p> Uncontrolled Hypertension : High blood pressure emerged as the leading culprit . " The majority of our stroke patients are hypertensive , " Professor Imarhiagbe stated , highlighting a worrying trend . He further elaborated on the various scenarios contributing to this issue , ranging from undiagnosed hypertension to neglected or inadequately controlled blood pressure . Alarmingly , some patients even discontinue their medication based on misinformation about a " cure . " He warns , " If you have high blood pressure that is left unattended to , you are potentially risking a stroke . " Irregular Heartbeats ( Atrial Fibrillation ) : Irregular heartbeats , particularly atrial fibrillation , also pose a significant risk . Professor Imarhiagbe explained that in this condition , the heart undergoes changes that can lead to clot formation . " A clot can dislodge from the heart and run up to the brain and block the blood pipes ... leading to stroke . " Uncontrolled Diabetes : Long-standing , poorly managed diabetes can wreak havoc on the blood vessels . " High blood sugar ... can contribute to causing plaque , otherwise called hardening of the arteries or atherosclerosis , " Professor Imarhiagbe stated . This narrowing of arteries restricts blood flow to the brain , increasing the risk of stroke.High Cholesterol Levels : Similar to diabetes , elevated cholesterol levels can contribute to the buildup of plaque in the arteries , obstructing blood flow to the brain.Professor Imarhiagbe stressed the importance of comprehensive health checks . " A regular complete check every year or once every six months is helpful , " he said , but cautioned against complacency . " All you know about your health is not enough , you can feel fine and not be well . The only way to know you are fine is to do a medical check on yourself . Otherwise , everybody sits on a time bomb , " he warns.Other , less common , but still significant modifiable risk factors include chronic alcohol abuse and tobacco smoking . Additionally , individuals with sickle cell disease face a lifelong increased risk of stroke . <p> Decoding The FLEAS : Recognising Subtle Signs Of Stroke <p> While cerebral thrombosis or embolism ( brain blood clots ) are underlying causes of stroke , Professor Imarhiagbe clarified that they are not signs in themselves . Instead , the causes lead to a variety of observable symptoms . He likened the relationship to a " chicken and egg story , " where the underlying cause triggers the signs that patients experience . <p> F -- Face : One side of the face may go numb or droop.L -- Limb : A limb ( arm or leg ) may experience weakness or numbness , typically on one side of the body.E -- Eyes : Dizziness or loss of balance can occur.A -- Arm : The arm can also become numb or weak.S -- Speech : Difficulty speaking , slurred speech , or an inability to understand speech are warning signs . <p> " Once anybody around you has any of these signs , it is time to call a doctor , " Professor Imarhiagbe emphasised . " It is time to seek help or call a doctor , or go to the hospital ... they are warning signs of stroke . " <p> He clarified that stroke symptoms are not gender-specific but are more related to age . Stroke occurring before the age of 45 is categorised as stroke in the young , with sickle cell disease being the most common cause in children . <p> Genetic Predisposition : Understanding Family History <p> Professor Imarhiagbe acknowledged the role of genetics in stroke risk . " There are persons who have a tendency to stroke . They have a genetic tendency to stroke , " he stated . He said the existence of specific genes that can predispose individuals to stroke . He encouraged people with a family history of stroke to be particularly vigilant about managing their risk factors . " If a parent suffers a stroke , the children should understand that it is a warning sign ... particularly if the risk factors for stroke are not attended to . Your biology may put you at the risk of a stroke , because you are your genes , as they say . " <p> Prevalence And Incidence : A Worrying Trend <p> The prevalence and incidence of stroke in Nigeria paint a concerning picture . Professor Imarhiagbe shared alarming statistics , revealing that the prevalence of stroke in Nigeria is " higher than 1,000 per 100,000 Nigerians , " potentially reaching as high as 1,200 per 100,000 . While incidence figures are lower , estimated to be between 100 and 360 per 100,000 , the high prevalence indicates a significant burden of existing stroke cases . Regional variations exist , with the Niger Delta region exhibiting some of the highest prevalence rates.When comparing Nigeria to other West African countries , Professor Imarhiagbe cautioned against drawing conclusions solely based on population size . He emphasised the need for standardised population figures to accurately compare stroke rates . <p> Alarmingly , Professor Imarhiagbe confirmed that stroke prevalence and incidence are indeed higher now than in the past . He attributed this increase to the rising prevalence of modifiable risk factors . " We are seeing more hepatitis than we ever did . We are seeing more diabetes than we ever did . The stress level is higher now . " He also highlighted the economic challenges that hinder individuals from accessing healthcare and managing their risk factors effectively . " People can no longer afford to buy their drugs to take off high blood pressure . People are finding it hard to maintain their blood sugar level . People are finding it hard right now to maintain their cholesterol levels . " He stated that the economic downturn affects the attention Nigerians give to their health " People are just looking for survival . So , it has a ripple effect on the health status of Nigerians or their well-being is affecting directly because of their economic status , " he said . <p> He pointed to a concerning trend of increased alcohol and tobacco uses as coping mechanisms for stress and depression further exacerbating the problem . " Most people are now trying to smoke away their frustration ... and then , these paper packs make alcohol very available now in the public , " he observed . <p> Challenges In Diagnosis And Treatment : A Race Against Time <p> Neurologists in Nigeria face numerous challenges in effectively diagnosing and treating stroke . Professor Imarhiagbe identified a critical obstacle : delayed presentation of patients to hospitals . " When it comes to stroke , time is gain , " he emphasised . " Most patients , especially most Africans , present very late . The time of presentation affects the outcome of treatment for stroke . " He lamented deeply ingrained cultural beliefs and misinformation that contribute to this delay . " Oyibo no get treatment for stroke , make you no let them give your pikin injection if he has stroke , " he quoted , highlighting common misconceptions that prevent patients from seeking timely medical intervention.He explained the importance of prompt treatment with clot-busting drugs , but stressed that these treatments are only effective within a narrow window of time , typically two to four and a half hours . " If you do n't come within that window , we ca n't bust that clots anymore . " He highlighted the limited availability of mechanical clot retrieval methods in Nigeria.Another significant challenge is the lack of readily available diagnostic tools , particularly CT scans and MRI machines , in many hospitals , forcing patients to travel long distances for diagnosis . <p> Government Intervention : A Call to Action <p> To address the increasing prevalence of stroke in Nigeria , Professor Imarhiagbe called for proactive government intervention . He emphasised the need for equipping hospitals , both regional and state level , with essential diagnostic equipment like CT scanners and MRI machines . This can improve access to timely diagnosis and treatment . <p> Immediate Action : What To Do When Stroke Strikes <p> Professor Imarhiagbe issued a clear and urgent call to action : " Report to the hospital immediately ! " He cautioned against relying on home remedies or delaying seeking professional medical help . " Do n't go to a chemist shop . Do n't apply local remedies . Do n't become a doctor that you are not overnight . " He addressed the misconception that prayer should replace medical intervention . " You can be praying for the man while you are taking him to the hospital . Rather than leave the man at home overnight and make us lose that window that we have to bust the clot . " <p> He reiterated the harmful effects of alcohol and tobacco use , urging individuals to abstain from both . <p> A Collective Effort To Combat Stroke <p> Stroke is a growing public health crisis in Nigeria , demanding a multi-faceted approach involving individual responsibility , improved healthcare infrastructure , and proactive government policies . By understanding and managing modifiable risk factors , recognising the subtle signs of stroke , seeking immediate medical attention , and dispelling harmful cultural beliefs , we can collectively work towards reducing the devastating impact of stroke on individuals , families , and the nation as a whole . Professor Imarhiagbe 's insights serve as a crucial reminder of the urgency and importance of addressing this looming pandemic head-on . <p> As President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his party , the All Progressive Congress ( APC ) , commemorate the administration 's two-year anniversary , the performance of his appointed ministers has come under increased scrutiny . The second edition of the assessment looks at the individual ministers ' key accomplishments , challenges , and overall impact across various sectors , providing a critical perspective on the administration 's progress towards fulfilling its promises and meeting the country 's pressing needs . Report by ROLAND OGBONNAYA , CHIDI UGWU , CHIBUZOR EMEJOR , TOYIN ADEBAYO and STELLA OMONA <p> The primary goal of this assessment is to determine their effectiveness in promoting policy implementation and managing resources for Nigeria 's development . <p> Dr. Adebayo Adedibu , Minister of Power and Energy <p> Reforms Boost Revenue As Blackouts , Consumer Woes Persist <p> The power sector in Nigeria , under the leadership of Dr. Adebayo Adedibu , Minister of Power and Energy , presents a paradox of two years into President Bola Tinubu 's administration . While the government boasts impressive reforms and revenue increases , widespread public dissatisfaction remains due to unreliable electricity supply . <p> Key reforms , such as the Electricity Act 2023 , aimed at decentralising power generation and distribution by allowing states to participate , and the new National Integrated Electricity Policy , designed to attract $122.2 billion in investments over 21 years , are bold . These policies aim to diversify energy sources beyond hydropower and gas-fired power plants , including solar , wind , hydrogen , and nuclear energy . <p> The government also highlights significant achievements , including a 70% revenue increase in 2024 , generating an additional N700 billion , and a record power generation capacity of 6,003 MW in March 2025 , a 40% increase over 2023 levels . These gains are attributed to cost-reflective tariff reforms and increased capacity , which allegedly reduced government subsidy shortfalls and improved financial sustainability . <p> However , this rosy picture contrasts starkly with consumers ' daily experiences . Despite revenue growth , Nigerians experience exploitative billing , illegal disconnections , a lack of metering , and frequent outages . Data demonstrates the magnitude of this issue : " 11 distribution companies received over 203,000 complaints in just six months in 2020 , and the situation is likely to worsen since then . " <p> Businesses are also feeling the impact of the unreliable grid . The high cost of alternative energy solutions puts additional strain on industries such as food and beverage and chemicals , which spend billions of dollars on self-generation . Furthermore , the national grid remains unstable , with multiple disruptions in early 2025 resulting in widespread blackouts . Consumers have protested , calling tariff increases due to poor service exploitative and threatening local business growth . <p> The underlying issue is an obsolete power infrastructure that has been neglected and underinvested for decades . Transmission grid flaws persist despite recent reforms . Metering remains a significant issue . As of December 31 , 2024 , only 6.29 million of the 13.5 million registered electricity customers across the 12 DisCos were metered , indicating a poor metering rate of 46.57% . <p> While Adelabu Tunji , Special Adviser on Strategic Communications and Media Relations to the Power Minister , maintains that " despite claims of stagnation , metering installations have been steadily progressing . As of December 2024 , a total of 5,502,460 customers were metered , accounting for approximately 55% of Nigeria 's 10,114,060 active electricity customers . In 2024 alone , 572,050 meters were installed , " leaving millions still focusing on arbitrary billing . <p> The government 's response is the Presidential Metering Initiative ( PMI ) , backed by ? 700 billion secured through the Federation Account Allocation Committee ( FAAC ) . The target is to deploy two million meters annually over the next five years . However , experts remain skeptical , claiming that " if efforts continue as they have in previous years , even with funding from the Federal Government through the Central Bank of Nigeria ( CBN ) , it will take more than a decade to meter the existing 7.2 million customers who are billed arbitrarily . " <p> Poor investments , insufficient gas supply , and inadequate infrastructure continue to plague Nigeria 's power sector , resulting in frequent blackouts . These failures have prompted calls for leadership changes , with stakeholders demanding the removal of Adebayo Adelabu , Minister of Power , and Sule Ahmed Abdulaziz , Managing Director of the Transmission Company of Nigeria ( TCN ) . <p> Organisations like the Nigerian Youth Treaty for Good Governance ( NYTGG ) have " highlighted the severe economic and social hardships caused by frequent blackouts , urging decisive government action , including Adelabu 's dismissal . " The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria ( HURIWA ) condemned the repeated grid failures as evidence of " gross incompetence , " and demanded Adelabu 's immediate removal . <p> Critics also question Adelabu 's suitability , claiming that " the government 's appointing a non-expert to such a critical role " is problematic . Chartered accountant Chief Okwudili Ijezie urged the president to fire Adelabu , recommending that experts such as Prof. Barth Nnaji be appointed instead . Ijezie linked improved power supply to economic growth and increased tax revenue . <p> The Federal government blames the repeated grid failures on a variety of factors , including ageing facilities , a lack of maintenance , insufficient investment , and sabotage . Kunle Olubiyo , President of the Nigeria Consumer Protection Network , highlights the issues of " obsolescence and weak infrastructure bedevilling activities of the sector in Nigeria , " emphasising the importance of regular maintenance of power infrastructure . <p> Olubiyo also criticised the budgetary allocation to the sector , " decrying the poor budgetary allocation to the sector amidst prevailing challenges , questioning the use of foreign loans . " He emphasised the importance of " ensuring efficient use of public funds to meet identified needs " and highlighted Nigeria 's energy poverty , stating that " having a peak generation transmission evacuation of 5,800 MW is the highest level of energy poverty any country can imagine . " <p> To summarise , while Minister Adedibu can point to some revenue increases and policy initiatives , the ongoing blackouts and consumer dissatisfaction highlight a significant gap between policy and practice . Addressing the fundamental issues of infrastructure decay , funding shortfalls , and regulatory challenges is critical to Nigeria 's long-term power supply stability and reliability . <p> Engr . David Umahi , Minister of Works <p> The performance of Engr . David Umahi , as Minister of Works , has been marked by both attention and controversy . A significant portion of his focus has been on the Lagos-Calabar coastal highway . Critics argue that this project has overshadowed the dire need to rehabilitate numerous dilapidated national highways across the country . While the coastal highway may have strategic economic benefits , the neglect of existing critical infrastructure has raised concerns about the minister 's priorities and resource allocation . <p> Senator Abubakar Kyari , Minister of Agriculture <p> Senator Abubakar Kyari 's tenure as Minister of Agriculture has coincided with Nigeria 's deteriorating food security crisis , despite the administration 's stated commitment to increasing agricultural production . According to reports from the World Food Programme ( WFP ) and the Food and Agriculture Organisation ( FAO ) , " 33 million people will face food insecurity in the June-August 2025 lean season , " a significant increase from the 26.5 million projected for the same period in 2024 . " The situation is driven by a combination of conflict , insecurity , high inflation , and climate change impacts , " the reports state . <p> In July 2023 , President Tinubu declared a state of emergency due to food insecurity , significantly increasing budgetary allocations to the agricultural sector . In 2023 , N228.4 billion was allocated ; this increased to N362.94 billion in 2024 and N826.5 billion in 2025 . <p> Kyari has numerous initiatives , including the distribution of over 1000 tractors , the strategic grain reserve and market price stabilisation , the distribution of 2,150,000 fertiliser bags , and the N1.5 trillion recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture ( BOA ) . Other initiatives include the establishment of the National Electronic Extension Platform ( NEEP ) , the revitalisation of the cooperative sector , a partnership with the World Bank to rehabilitate 200,000 kilometres of rural roads , and the provision of subsidised agricultural inputs to farmers through the National Agricultural Growth Scheme Agro-Pocket ( NAGS-AP ) . <p> Senator Abubakar Kyari stated , " The ministry has been working assiduously to ensure food and nutrition security for the country in line with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu 's Renewed Hope Agenda . " <p> The administration has also launched a dry season farming initiative on 500,000 hectares of farmland , funded by the African Development Bank with $134 million to encourage year-round farming . <p> Despite these efforts , the agricultural sector 's contribution to GDP in the fourth quarter of 2024 was 25.59 per cent , with a 1.76 per cent growth rate , indicating limited progress in addressing the food crisis . <p> The challenges are significant . Insecurity across the country , particularly in food-producing states , continues to stymie agricultural activity . " Insecurity , climate change , and poor implementation of government policies and programmes are the sector 's bane , " stated Arc Ibrahim Kabir , National President of the All Farmers Association of Nigeria ( AFAN ) . <p> Climate change is also a major threat , as extreme weather events exacerbate food production challenges . Food inflation remains a major contributor to overall inflation . In May 2025 , the food inflation rate was 21.14 per cent year on year , down sharply from 40.66 per cent in the same month last year . <p> However , " on a month-on-month basis , however , food inflation rose to 2.19 per cent in May from 2.06 per cent in April , driven by increases in the prices of yam , cassava , maize flour , sweet potatoes , fresh pepper , and ogbono , " according to the National Bureau of Statistics . <p> While Minister Kyari has overseen several initiatives aimed at increasing agricultural production , the ongoing rise in food insecurity raises concerns about the effectiveness and implementation of the policies . Addressing insecurity , improving climate resilience , and ensuring the effective implementation of agricultural programs are critical to making tangible progress in food security under Minister Kyari 's leadership . <p> Yusuf Tuggar , Minister for Foreign Affairs <p> As President Bola Tinubu 's administration nears its two-year mark , Nigeria 's foreign policy , led by Minister of Foreign Affairs Amb Maitama Tuggar , has received both praise and criticism . While Tuggar has been praised for his efforts to promote Nigeria on the international stage , some have questioned the administration 's approach , particularly regarding the ECOWAS bloc . <p> Tuggar has played an important role in promoting President Tinubu 's foreign policy direction , which is defined by a strategic shift towards economic diplomacy based on the " 4D doctrine of democracy , development , demography , and diaspora . " <p> Dr. Jeffrey Isima acknowledges that Tuggar " has done well in terms of projecting Nigeria 's natural , demographic , and economic potentials abroad , " but emphasises the importance of first building internal capacity before being reckoned with internationally .
